title: Chosen fibre-product Cech complex agrees with Mathlib on a category with finite wide pullbacks
statement: Let C be a category with finite wide pullbacks, U an object, I a set, and f_i : V_i → U an arbitrary family of arrows. Let S be any chosen-product SiteCechComplex V f [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex]. For any abelian presheaf F [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-presheaves-evaluation-exact], the cochain complex S.complex F is isomorphic to the Mathlib cechComplexFunctor for the family Over.mk f_i in Over U, applied to (Over.forget U).op ⋙ F [def-weil-pbc-cech-complex]. The sections of F and the index set I live in the same arbitrary universe; the objects and arrows of C can have different universes. No covering, sheaf or injectivity condition is imposed.

source.place: Section 03AK, Definition 03AM (definition-cech); projection-compatible product comparison in step 3 of lem-weil-pbc-injective-etale-module-cech-h1, written out by C1. Mathlib Sites/SheafCohomology/Cech.lean and Limits/FormalCoproducts/Cech.lean fix the comparison model.

proof.text: For each tuple t : Fin(p+1) → I, the product of Over.mk(f(t k)) in Over U represents the iterated fibre product of the V(t k). Compare its projections with S.pr p t using the two universal properties. There are unique projection-compatible maps in both directions; their composites have the identity projections and therefore equal the identities. This gives an isomorphism of the underlying objects of C.

Apply contravariant F to these isomorphisms. The universal property of the categorical product of abelian groups identifies it with the abelian group of tuples of sections used by S.cochains F p. The component restriction maps thus give inverse degreewise group isomorphisms. For I empty, all tuple-index sets Fin(p+1) → I are empty, so both degree objects are zero; the same construction applies.

For an omitted-factor index map, both routes around the comparison square have identical projections to all retained factors. The product universal property makes them equal. Applying F shows that degreewise comparison commutes with each signed restriction summand. Summing gives commutation with the differential. The inverse maps also commute, and the degreewise inverse equations produce an isomorphism of cochain complexes.

Projection uniqueness gives compatibility with every index map, and differential_sum gives compatibility with the alternating differential. from.place: Step 3: identify the chosen-fibre-product complex with Mathlib cechComplexFunctor using projection-compatible product isomorphisms

lean.statement:
theorem mathlib_complex_iso_exists
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [HasFiniteWidePullbacks C]
    {U : C} {I : Type w} (V : I → C) (f : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U)
    (S : SiteCechComplex V f) (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{w}) :
    Nonempty (S.complex F ≅
      (cechComplexFunctor fun i : I ↦ Over.mk (f i)).obj ((Over.forget U).op ⋙ F))
